math_plain: Scores word importance by combining multiple model opinions and selects the top-ranked words to create adversarial text that fools AI systems.
why_math: Different models have different blindnesses; averaging their agreement reveals true vulnerabilities no single model captures. Combining weak signals this way finds robust attack patterns.

math_plain: Selects a tiny subset of the data for training by optimizing which samples matter most, while removing noisy or unreliable interactions.
why_math: Most data points contribute equally to improving the model; identifying and keeping only the high-value samples lets you train with far less data. Removing noise ensures those kept samples actually improve rather than mislead.

why_math: Developers who frequently interact sit close together in collaboration space; measuring distances and densities in this space reveals community structure and health without needing to manually define what healthy means.

math_plain: Ranks items by combining probabilities from sub-rankings instead of ranking all items at once, using a structural decomposition to aggregate sub-scores.
why_math: Predicting the full ranking order is costly; breaking it into smaller sub-rankings you can compute in one pass, then using algebraic decomposition to combine them, gives you ranking predictions without the exponential cost.

math_plain: Proves user identity by checking a mathematical signature without revealing the user's secret key, using discrete logarithm hard problems.
why_math: If only the user knows the secret key, only they can generate signatures that pass the mathematical check; the check's security rests on a problem so hard it can't be inverted, making forgery impossible.

why_math: How fast users act between clicks reveals their interest intensity; grouping users by similar time-gap patterns finds neighbors with matching intent, making next-item prediction accurate without needing to know absolute timestamps.

why_math: Models sometimes hallucinate; if you can detect when the model is guessing versus confident, you can trust its confident answers and fall back to experts only when needed, minimizing costly expert involvement while keeping quality high.

math_plain: Defends against poisoned data by transforming embeddings to make poisoned samples stick out, then voting to remove them based on majority agreement.
why_math: Poisoned samples are rare and different; transforming to make those differences obvious, then using majority voting as a robustness check, filters them out because a single poison can't outweigh the majority of clean data.

math_plain: Predicts when users are surprised by search results using eye-movement patterns like how long they look and how often they refocus.
why_math: Surprise changes attention behavior in measurable ways; looking longer at unexpected content is statistically higher than at expected content, so sustained eye metrics capture the mismatch signal reliably.
